config.title: useWindowSize

intro.title: useWindowSize
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called useWindowSize that tracks the current width and height of the browser window. You will learn how to use the useState and useEffect hooks to manage and update state based on window resize events. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the browser's window API. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to create reusable hooks that respond to dynamic changes in the user's viewport.
intro.usecase: The useWindowSize hook is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes in real-time. Developers use this pattern in dashboards to rearrange charts and widgets when users resize their browser windows, or in e-commerce product filters that switch between dropdowns and sidebar layouts based on available space. It's also crucial for media galleries that adjust image grid columns, and for navigation menus that transform between horizontal bars and hamburger menus dynamically as the viewport changes.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook that tracks browser window dimensions
Initialize state variables to store current width and height values
Construct an event listener to respond to window resize events
Apply cleanup logic to remove event listeners when the component unmounts
Integrate the useWindowSize hook into a functional component
Render dynamic UI elements that respond to window size changes
Configure TypeScript interfaces to define the hook's return type

steps.title: Create the useWindowSize custom hook function
steps.instruction: Create a function named useWindowSize that returns the WindowSize type. Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Start by writing 'function useWindowSize(): WindowSize' or 'const useWindowSize = (): WindowSize =>'. Remember to include the return type annotation.

successCriteria: The useWindowSize function is declared with a return type of WindowSize.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Check that you've named it 'useWindowSize' and specified that it returns the WindowSize type.

steps.title: Initialize state for window dimensions
steps.instruction: Inside your useWindowSize function, call useState with an initial value containing width and height properties (both numbers) and destructure it into windowSize and setWindowSize.
steps.hint: Use useState<WindowSize> to type the state. Initialize with reasonable default dimensions like width: window.innerWidth and height: window.innerHeight.

// Example: state initialization with an object
const [user, setUser] = useState<{name: string, age: number}>({name: '', age: 0});
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWindowSize hook will have a state variable windowSize and a setter setWindowSize, both typed as WindowSize.
successCriteria: useState is called with an initial WindowSize object, and the result is destructured into windowSize and setWindowSize.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize hook, create a function named handleResize that updates the windowSize state with the current window dimensions.
steps.hint: The function should access window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight, then call setWindowSize with those values.

The function calls setWindowSize with an object containing width and height from window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight

steps.instruction: Wrap the existing handleResize function in a useCallback hook with an empty dependency array to memoize it.
steps.hint: Use useCallback to wrap the function definition. The empty dependency array ensures the function reference stays the same across renders.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleResize function is memoized using useCallback to prevent unnecessary re-creations on every render.
successCriteria: handleResize is wrapped in useCallback with an empty dependency array.

steps.title: Add resize event listener with useEffect
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook inside the useWindowSize function to set up a 'resize' event listener that calls handleResize and cleans up on unmount.
steps.hint: Use useEffect with an empty dependency array to run only on mount. Inside, add the event listener to the window object and return a cleanup function that removes it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook will be added to listen for window resize events and update the state accordingly, with proper cleanup.
successCriteria: useEffect is added with an empty dependency array, adds a 'resize' event listener that calls handleResize, and returns a cleanup function that removes the listener.
